overall: The AG found the Topsfield Collins Center Working Group is a public body subject to the OML (letter dated February 20, 2018), that it violated the law by failing to post notice and keep minutes, and ordered compliance plus minutes within 30 days.

allegations.summary: Working Group contended it is not a public body: it is not empowered to act collectively and was appointed only to advise the town administrator.
allegations.key_passage: For the foregoing reasons, we conclude that the Working Group is a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Working Group met without posting notice of its meetings.
allegations.key_passage: The Working Group did not post notice of these meetings

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Working Group kept no formal minutes of its meetings.
allegations.key_passage: while the town administrator took notes during the meetings, no formal minutes were kept

allegations.summary: A two-member subquorum gathering of the Working Group was examined to see whether it triggered Open Meeting Law requirements.
allegations.key_passage: Because this gathering did not consist of a quorum of the Working Group, it did not trigger the requirements of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Within 30 days of receipt of the letter, create and approve minutes for all Working Group meetings.
Upon completing the minutes, notify the AG's office of compliance in writing under 940 CMR 29.07(4).
remedy_passage: We order the Working Group's immediate and future compliance with the law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
